sources: Greenspoon, Krieger, Sender, Rosenberg, Bar-On, Moran, Milo et al. (2023), 'The global biomass of wild mammals', PNAS 120(10); Weizmann Institute press release (Feb 2023): wild land mammals about 20 million tonnes, wild marine mammals about 40 million tonnes, domesticated mammals about 630 million tonnes (livestock about 30x wild land mammals); wild land mammals less than 10% of humanity's combined weight.

Per person: 20,000,000 t / 8.2 billion people (2026) = about 2.4 kg. 'Most mammals live on farms' by weight: 630 Mt livestock > humans (< 10x wild land, i.e. > 200 Mt) + wild land + marine (Bar-On et al. 2018, PNAS, also put livestock at about 60% of mammal biomass).
